Stocks are rebounding Monday morning after the worst week since 2020. The sources I found disagree on some numbers, so treat the moves as approximate. All of it is premarket or early trading, and I couldn't confirm anything from the 8:30 AM CT open.

**Where things stand**
- Last week the S&P 500 fell 8.6% and the Nasdaq Composite fell about 10%, its worst week since March 2020. The Dow fell about 8%.
- Friday's closes: S&P 500 at 6,910.39 (down 3.7%), Nasdaq at 22,617.73 (down 5.3%) and Dow at 48,147.33 (down 1.9%).
- The S&P 500 and Dow are both in correction, more than 10% off their records. The Nasdaq Composite has lost its 2026 gain, and the Nasdaq-100 briefly hit bear-market territory intraday.
- The VIX jumped from about 20 to above 37 over the week.
- Monday futures are up about 2% to 3%: Dow roughly 1.8%, S&P 500 about 2.5%, Nasdaq-100 over 3%.

**The stories driving prices**
1. **The AI trade unwinding.** This is the main story. Roughly $8 trillion has left US stocks since the Oct. 6 peak. The premarket bounce is concentrated in the names that fell hardest. Chips are up (AMD +9%, Micron +6%, Broadcom +5.7%). AI cloud and data-center names are up about 10% (CoreWeave, IREN, Nebius, Applied Digital).
2. **Nvidia and Jensen Huang.** Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12. Nvidia fell about 14% Friday amid a reported alleged Chinese spy scandal. One report says Reuters had an SEC accounting probe, which I couldn't confirm in the CNBC piece. Trump posted that he hopes the board rehires Huang, and the board reportedly did. Fox puts Nvidia up more than 28% premarket, while another source says up to 9.7%. CNBC's piece didn't report the Huang rehiring, so I'd treat it as unconfirmed until the open.
3. **Anthropic's IPO.** It listed as "ANT" last week, raising about $81.3B at $83 a share, and opened well above that on Thursday. It then faded, falling 8.5% Friday, and is mixed to slightly higher Monday. Its record listing came in the same week as the tech rout. This is its first full week as a public company.
4. **The Fed may hike.** CME FedWatch shows about a 96% chance of a 25 basis point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting. That is a hike, not a cut. October PCE inflation is due Wednesday at 8:30 AM ET (7:30 AM CT), and it is the main data point of the week.
5. **Deals and earnings.**
   - CrowdStrike is down 7% after announcing a $43.9B deal to buy Zscaler. Zscaler is up 15% or more.
   - Dell and Best Buy report Tuesday, followed by HPE, Workday, Autodesk, Analog Devices and Deere. Dell's AI backlog and server margins are the focus.
6. **Macro and global.**
   - Brent crude is down about 4.5% and gold is above $3,620.
   - Asia didn't follow the US bounce. Korea's Kospi fell about 3.3%, with SK Hynix a big loser, while European tech rallied.
   - Markets are closed Thursday and close early Friday, so thin trading could exaggerate moves.

**The debate**
- **Bulls:** Goldman's Sharon Bell says "we're not at those excessive valuations." Holiday-week seasonality has historically leaned positive, and the AI names have been oversold.
- **Bears:** A rate hike is coming, the VIX is above 37, and the Nvidia governance and China questions are unresolved. Cole Smead's view is "when the home is on fire, you don't go rushing in." Questions remain over whether Monday's bounce will last.

**What to check at the open**
- Whether Nvidia's Huang news is confirmed.
- Whether the bounce holds past the first hour.
- Whether Wednesday's PCE moves the hike odds.

Revenue was $1.30B, down 1.3% and in line. FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.50–8.00 (midpoint $7.75) came in about 7% below consensus. The sources disagree on the consensus figure: StockStory has the miss at 7.3%, and Tickeron has consensus near $8.01 and also calls Q4 EPS a miss against $2.31. FY27 revenue guidance of $5.45–5.65B was above consensus.

**What the guide reflects:**
- FY26 adjusted EPS of $8.24 included about $75M of revenue and $1.05 per share of VA disability-exam incentives, earned in the first three quarters. In Q4 the VA customer directed a change to those incentives, and FY27 assumes none. Excluding them, FY26 was about $7.19, so the midpoint implies about 8% growth.
- FY26 free cash flow was $69M, against guidance of $425–475M. DSO rose to 93 days from 62. Management calls it timing and says more than $330M was collected after year-end. FY27 free cash flow guidance of $700–800M assumes DSO returns to 60–70 days.
- Maximus closed the Agile Defense acquisition on 11-18 for $660M, plus up to $50M tied to revenue milestones. It added $295M of term loans. Pro forma leverage is about 2.3x, inside the 2–3x target range. FY27 includes about ten months of Agile revenue.
- FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance is $690–725M (about 12.8% margin), below FY26's $741M.
- The $400M buyback authorization is fully available, with about $200M of repurchases expected in FY27. The $0.33 dividend is payable 11-30, and the 11-13 record date has already passed.
- Backlog fell 10% to $13.8B, and federal backlog fell 30%. Trailing book-to-bill is 0.5x, though Q4 was about 1.0x, helped by an $800M+ Medicaid renewal. The recompete win rate is about 89%.
- Federal segment margin guidance is 14–15%, against 18.1% in FY26 (Panabee).

- **Cash collection:** Evidence that DSO is falling would address the credibility problem. No scheduled catalyst. The next earnings report is in February.
- **VA disability-exam recompete:** The final RFP was expected in November, with award around April–May 2027 and a start on 7-1-2027. Tickeron says the new vehicle is five years, not ten, and puts bids due in mid-December. I could not confirm the bid date in a primary source. Maximus's VES unit holds Regions 1–4 now. A new RFP or a bid-timing headline could move the stock.

- **Analyst moves:** I found no post-earnings price-target changes. Coverage is thin, with an average target of about $92.50 (as of 11-18) against a $64 share price. Any cuts or upgrades would be new information.

- The 5% drop was not in doubt, but the sources disagree on the exact close.

The other sources I opened were the SEC press release, Panabee, StockStory, Tickeron, a SamSearch page on the VA recompete, and a Finviz article on the incentive pause. **BJ (BJ's Wholesale Club) research for the 1–10 session decision, as of 9:00 AM CT on 2026-11-23**

**Bottom line:** The drop looks like a second leg of selling after Friday's earnings drop, not new bad news. I found no news dated today. The business results were strong, but the market is discounting them as low quality. The next few sessions are probably a fight between dip buyers and holders who sell the rally.

**What happened (Q3 FY26, reported Fri 11/20; call held the same day)**
- **Sales:** Comparable sales excluding gas rose 4.1%, against about 2.9% expected. Including gas they rose 13.5%. Net sales were $6.1B, up 17.7% (the $6.28B figure in other coverage is a different measure). Comparable traffic rose 6%, the highest since 2020, during a roughly six-week 42nd-anniversary promotion that management estimates added about 1 point to comps.
- **Earnings:** Adjusted EPS was $1.73, against a $1.26 consensus (FactSet). The beat is mostly a one-time item. SG&A included a credit-card interchange settlement of about $240M, offset by about $95M of spending in the quarter. Management said over $150M of the settlement went into promotions, pay and advertising.
- **Margin:** Merchandise gross margin fell about 170 basis points, with about $56M of the promotion cost blamed. Gross profit dollars rose 1% to $1.02B. Management says margin excluding the promotion was on target and similar to Q2.
- **Guidance:** Full-year adjusted EPS guidance went to $5.10–5.30 from $4.60–4.80 (consensus was about $4.74). The comp range excluding gas is 2.5–3.0%. Most of the EPS raise appears to be the settlement. I could not confirm the exact split.
- **Membership:** Fee income rose 9.5% to $138.4M, with more than 8.5M members. Management expects growth to slow toward about 7.5%. Gas gallons were up about 11% on a comparable basis, against an industry decline of about 5%.
- **Q4 and 2027:** Management did not cut Q4 investment plans. It expects some pull-forward in general merchandise (outerwear, mixers), and mild weather slowed winter apparel. CEO Eddy declined to guide 2027. BJ's laps the settlement and most of the Q3 investment, and flagged diesel, medical and gasoline costs. Nearly 30 new clubs are planned for 2027–28.

**Price action**
- Shares were down about 7.1% pre-market Friday at $102.85, which implies a prior close near $110.7. Backing out from your screen, Friday closed near $104.8, so today's move is another 4.3% down.

- The May 22 report also produced an 8% one-day drop, to about $86.68. The stock then recovered to roughly $110 by Friday's close. Dip buyers have worked here before.
- Other sources, not independently confirmed: Simply Wall St's $109 narrative fair value, about 24 times earnings, and heavy insider selling as a flagged risk.

**What could move the stock over the next 1–10 sessions**
- **Down:**
  - The earnings-quality argument. Analysts will likely keep stressing the one-time settlement and the tougher 2027 comparison.
  - The 50-day average ($101.98) has been lost.
  - Peers cited freight, fuel and price-investment costs (TJX, Target), which supports the margin concern.
  - I found no analyst target changes dated after the report. Cuts could come in the first week.
